By not incorporating the user’s constraints early, the orchestrator set the entire chain of actions on a shaky foundation, leading to a cascade of ineffective searches, repeated failures to locate menus, and ultimately a wrong answer.
A corrected version of Step 1 would formulate a precise search query that includes all user constraints (e.g., "vegan main under $15 dine‑in Washington Square Park"), verify that the search results cover all close-by venues, and explicitly include the known target restaurant (Shanghai villa) if possible. It would also outline a fallback plan to use direct restaurant websites or reliable aggregator sites when search results are incomplete. This would prevent the initial mis‑direction that caused the subsequent failures.
